name: Ireland
hook: Patrick, the shamrock and the black stuff: the Irish answers that keep coming back.

facts.label: St. Patrick
facts.statement: St. Patrick was taken to Ireland as a slave in the early 400s, escaped, and returned as a missionary; his feast day, March 17, is a national holiday.

facts.label: the shamrock
facts.statement: St. Patrick used the shamrock to explain the Trinity, and it remains Ireland's national symbol.

facts.label: the potato
facts.statement: Potatoes became Ireland's staple crop, and in the 1840s late blight destroyed the harvest and caused the Great Famine.

facts.label: Dublin
facts.statement: Dublin is the Republic's capital and, with Cork, one of its only two cities with more than 100,000 people.

facts.label: Belfast
facts.statement: Belfast, Northern Ireland's capital, sits on the River Lagan and was chartered in 1613.

facts.label: the Shannon
facts.statement: The Shannon is the longest river in Ireland and the British Isles, and its name is also Ireland's main airport.

facts.label: Guinness
facts.statement: The Guinness family gave Dublin its first Lord Mayor and founded Ireland's most famous brewery.
